questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of the cell membrane?
options: It provides structural rigidity to the plant cell
It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell
It is the site of protein synthesis
It stores the genetic information of the cell
questions.model_answer: The cell membrane controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell. It is selectively permeable, allowing certain molecules to pass while restricting others.
questions.verification_note: Model answer is directly supported by the source chunk's description of selective permeability of the cell membrane.
questions.explanation_en: The cell membrane is a selectively permeable barrier made of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. It regulates what enters and exits the cell — allowing oxygen, water, and nutrients in while keeping harmful substances out.

questions.question: Differentiate between a cell wall and a cell membrane. Give two points of difference.
questions.model_answer: Cell wall: (1) Present only in plant cells, fungi, and bacteria. (2) Made of cellulose in plants; it is rigid and provides structural support. Cell membrane: (1) Present in all living cells (plant and animal). (2) Made of a phospholipid bilayer; it is flexible and selectively permeable.
questions.verification_note: Both points of difference are explicitly stated in the source chunk, which contrasts cell wall composition and distribution with those of the cell membrane.
questions.explanation_en: The cell wall is a stiff outer layer found only outside the cell membrane in plant cells. It is made of cellulose and gives shape and protection. The cell membrane, by contrast, is present in every living cell and is a flexible phospholipid bilayer that controls what passes in and out.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for producing energy (ATP) in the cell through cellular respiration?
questions.model_answer: Mitochondria are responsible for producing ATP through the process of cellular respiration. They are known as the powerhouse of the cell.
questions.verification_note: The source chunk mentions mitochondria and cellular respiration in passing but does not explicitly state that mitochondria produce ATP or use the phrase 'powerhouse of the cell'. The model answer goes beyond what the retrieved passage directly supports.
questions.explanation_en: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, converting glucose and oxygen into ATP (energy), carbon dioxide, and water. They have a double membrane structure with inner folds called cristae that increase the surface area for this process.
